what: Celestica builds electronic hardware for other companies. Its fastest-growing work is network switches and racks for AI data centres, designed either to a customer's specification or to its own designs sold under the Celestica name.
customers: Hyperscale cloud operators, networking equipment companies, aerospace and defence contractors, and industrial and healthcare manufacturers.
money: network switches, servers and storage for data centres
aerospace, defence, industrial, healthcare and capital equipment
moat: Its own high-speed networking switch designs, which turn a contract manufacturer into a product company with better margins, plus engineering relationships with hyperscalers.
risks: Gross margin of 12% is thin, as is normal in contract manufacturing
A few hyperscale customers account for a large share of revenue
Orders can be cut quickly if a customer changes its data centre plans
The shares have risen sharply and trade at a high multiple for the sector
opportunities: Revenue grew about 28% last year and about 20% a year over three years
Return on invested capital of 28% with cash of $4 billion against $1 billion of debt
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
watch: Connectivity and Cloud Solutions revenue growth and customer concentration.
